title: Refusal
description: The body of a refusal the control plane answers an adapter's request with, application/json. The codes an adapter meets: 401 unauthorized, one uniform unsigned answer for everything about who is asking: a missing signature, or one that is not 64 bytes of strict base64url; a well-formed signature that fails to verify, an S at or above the group order included; a missing or malformed access key id; an unknown or revoked access key, or a key of another kind; a GET's X-Qory-Timestamp that is missing, not a decimal integer, or more than 300 seconds from the control plane's clock, either way; a POST's time more than 300 seconds from it, either way; and a replay, a request whose signature it has already seen, under the replay rule of definitions.schema.json. It tells the adapter nothing about which cause applied, and an adapter never takes it as the access key being revoked; 403 connection_unknown, a request other than a sources/disconnect naming a connection_id that the control plane does not hold for this adapter, whether unknown, removed, as after its organisation is removed, or another adapter's, with one signed body for all of these, so the answer tells nothing about other adapters, and a pending connection is answered 403 connection_unknown on every request but POST /v1/connections/disconnect, which ends it with the signed 204, and POST /v1/sources/disconnect, which is answered with the signed 204 and changes nothing (sources-disconnect.schema.json): only a 403 connection_unknown that lasts after the adapter's retries, and only for a live connection, counts as the connection ended, and definitions.schema.json says how the adapter treats it and how it ends a pending link; 403 forbidden, a request the access key may not make, whatever the connection, which never ends a connection; 400 bad_request, for two causes alone: a signing header sent twice, X-Qory-Access-Key-Id, X-Qory-Instance-Id, X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519 or X-Qory-Timestamp, or an X-Qory-Instance-Id that is absent or outside its pattern; 400 unsupported_contract_version, an X-Qory-Contract-Version that is missing, sent twice, not a decimal integer, or a revision the control plane does not serve; 400 invalid_request, a body that breaks its schema, an integer written with a fraction or an exponent outside the description member of POST /v1/adapter, or an object that repeats a member, at any depth; 404 not_found, a route the control plane does not serve; 413 payload_too_large, a request over 1 MiB; 415 unsupported_media_type, a POST whose Content-Type is not application/json, while a GET carries no body and no Content-Type and is never refused 415; 409 collection_not_linked, a request for items or comments that is answered by a collection not linked, or that names a collection_ref the control plane holds no collection for or an item_ref it holds no item for (definitions.schema.json); 409 connection_ended, a request of a connection that ended, or for a collection that ended with one, final for that connection: the adapter drops that connection's collections from its state; 409 connection_suspended, a request of a connection whose organisation is out of use for now, or for a live collection of one, not final: the adapter changes no state and sends the request again on its periodic check; the control plane decides rights first, from the access key and the action alone, before it looks up any connection: a request the key may not make is answered 403 forbidden whatever its connection_id, so a key cannot tell held ids from others by its rights; it then decides 403 connection_unknown, for a request naming a connection_id, then connection_ended, then connection_suspended, then collection_not_linked, except on POST /v1/sources/disconnect, where connection_unknown and connection_ended do not apply: a ref with no live collection under the connection_id it names is answered with the signed 204, whatever that connection_id, and only connection_suspended applies (sources-disconnect.schema.json), and on POST /v1/connections/disconnect, where the order is 403, then connection_ended, and connection_suspended does not apply: a disconnect of a suspended connection is answered with the signed 204 and ends the connection; 429 rate_limited, with Retry-After, the seconds the adapter waits before it sends the request again, built anew, as definitions.schema.json describes a retry. A 401 is always unsigned. A 413, 415 or 400 bad_request may be unsigned, because the control plane may decide them before it verifies the request's signature. Every other answer is signed, and an adapter acts on no other unsigned answer. On an unsigned 401, 413, 415 or 400 bad_request, the adapter changes no state: no cursor, no run, no key. It treats the request as failed and sends it again, built anew as definitions.schema.json describes a retry, with backoff. It never takes a 401 as revocation, and never splits or drops items because of an unsigned 413. An unsigned 429 is not a 429: the adapter ignores its Retry-After and backs off as it does for any failed request. A signed answer is signed as definitions.schema.json describes. A member this schema does not define is refused.
